newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas offers to help grounded kiwis.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas offers to help grounded kiwis.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Monday it would offer special fares to passengers stranded in Australia and New Zealand after budget-airline Kiwi International Airlines said earlier on Monday it would go into voluntary liquidation.
One way fares would be offered to Kiwi passengers to help them return home, Qantas Executive General Manager Commercial Geoff Dixon said in a statement.

"We will make seats available for A$150 per adult and A$100 for children one-way in both directions between East Coast Australian capitals and the relevant New Zealand cities served by Qantas," Qantas said.
Those passengers stranded in New Zealand would be charged NZ$150 per adult and A$100 per child, Qantas said.
"The fares between New Zealand and Perth will be A$250 for adults and A$150 for children because of the greater distances involved," it said.
Again those passengers stuck in New Zealand flying to Perth would pay NZ$250 per adult and NZ$150 per child.
Qantas said it had formulated the rescue package after discussions with Kiwi International.
Kiwi started up from a travel business and expanded to a charter operation.
Its successful operation prompted Air New Zealand Ltd to set up its own budget-charter operation, Freedom Air.
Kiwi said earlier on Monday Auckland chartered accountants Price Waterhouse had been asked to appoint a liquidator to handle the liquidation.

The two-year old airline headquartered in the central North Island town of Hamilton had been hurt by events such as the grounding of flights due to the ash cloud from Mount Ruapehu volcano, an air traffic controllers' curfew, fog and mechanical breakdowns.
